- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and model rises sharply, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.  
- If model shows strong upward trend after a recent dip, check for mean reversion; if true outcome reverses, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7–14 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows sharp decline after model peak, model likely overreacted; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating 0.00/0.67/1.00 cycles, model may be overfitting to sentiment; use sentiment as a multiplier (0.8–1.2) rather than direct input.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently 5–8% above true outcome, apply “mean reversion bias” — subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 10–15 days unless sentiment strongly supports upside.  
- If sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model may be underestimating risk; add 1–3% to forecast to account for potential volatility or policy surprises.
